**Reasoning summary:** Using the drag profile reconstructed from the 24 drop/bounce measurements (near-floor hump b≈0.19, valley b≈0.044 at z≈0.24, rising to b≈0.20 near z≈1.1), I integrated the launched trajectory: vertical fall from centre z=0.855 m reaches z≈0.18 m at t=0.74 s (first impact only occurs at ≈0.82 s, so no bounce yet), while the horizontal velocity is strongly damped (∫b/m dt≈0.65), giving x≈0.53 m instead of the vacuum 0.78 m. The image matching both the low altitude and the shortened horizontal travel is **B**.

B

A

**Reasoning summary:** From the drop/bounce record, b(z) peaks (~0.20 kg/s) near z≈1.1 m, dips (~0.045) near z≈0.25 m, and rises again (~0.19) near the floor. Launching from centre height 1.105 m with vₓ=0.75 m/s, the fall to first impact takes ≈1.01–1.04 s (matching the h≈1.0–1.2 drop timings), during which ∫b dt ≈ 0.14 kg·s/m² gives strong horizontal damping (factor e^(−∫b/m dt) ≈ 0.25 at impact), so x ≈ 0.28 m at impact. The rebound (v≈1.6–1.7 m/s up, e=0.8) apexes near centre height ≈0.33–0.35 m at t≈1.45 s; at t=1.54 s the ball is just past apex at z≈0.32 m, having drifted only ≈0.07 m further horizontally (total x ≈ 0.35–0.36 m ≈ 205 px right of launch). This matches choice A's position (≈0.36 m right, ≈0.32 m centre height).

A

D

**Reasoning summary:** From the drop/bounce record, b(z) is small near the floor hump zone, minimal at z≈0.24, and rises to a broad peak (≈0.2 kg/s) around z≈1.0–1.4, falling off above z≈2. Launching from centre height z₀ = 1.625 + 0.03 = 1.655 m with vₓ = 1.15 m/s, the ball falls through the high-drag band: its vertical speed saturates near mg/b ≈ 1.2–1.5 m/s, so after 1.05 s it has fallen only ≈0.85–0.9 m (z ≈ 0.78–0.80 m), well above the vacuum prediction (which would put it at the floor). Horizontally, ∫b dt ≈ 0.2 kg·s/m gives an exponential damping factor exp(−10∫b dt) that shrinks vₓ to ≈0.2 m/s by t = 1 s, yielding a total horizontal travel of ≈0.44 m (≈0.45 m), not the 1.21 m of a drag-free flight. No impact occurs before 1.05 s (first impact ≈1.46 s), so restitution is irrelevant. The snapshot matching z ≈ 0.8 m with x ≈ 0.44 m is choice D.

**Reasoning summary:** From the bounce calibration, a release at ~1.875 m clearance impacts at t₁ ≈ 1.55–1.60 s with rebound apex centre height ≈ 0.40 m (rebound clearance ≈ 0.365–0.39 m). The ascent takes ≈ 0.45–0.55 s, so at t = 2.13 s the ball is at or just past its first rebound apex — i.e., centre height ≈ 0.40–0.42 m, ruling out the higher positions in A–C. Horizontally, the strong drag (b/m ≈ 1.5–2 s⁻¹ along much of the path, especially the near‑floor hump and the mid‑height peak) reduces the 0.80 m/s launch to a total displacement of only ≈ 0.45–0.50 m, matching the smallest horizontal offset. Both criteria pick the lowest, least‑advanced ball.

D
